title: Tarkovsky’s Stalker (1979) and it’s possible theme

commenti.body:
Andrei always was a bit coy with the meaning of his films. I think it was partly a defense mechanism as evidenced here: 

*Upon its release the film's reception was less than favorable. Officials at Goskino, were critical of the film. On being told that Stalker should be faster and more dynamic,

Tarkovsky replied:
The film needs to be slower and duller at the start so that the viewers who walked into the wrong theatre have time to leave before the main action starts.*

But also given his ethereal creative genius quality it's fitting too. His interviews always leave me feeling a but perplexed but in the most uplifting way naturally.

Sigh.

Personally, the most compelling aspect to Stalker was the distortion of time to convey the zone's supernatural effect. Time itself stretches as if it were a substance the longer that the scene plays out, creating a sort of dream-like quality. My favourite example is at 1:06 where we see water splashing in a well in slow motion, and then 40 minutes later we see the writer drop a brick into the same well. An explanation is offered at one point by the stalker who points out that time and space are all affected in the zone, causing things to "change every minute".

Here is what Tarkovsky had to say about it:

‘Film fixes reality in a sense of time—it’s a way of conserving time. No other art form can fix and stop time like this. Film is a mosaic made up of time.’

On my most recent rewatch, my third, a new interpretation I had for the film was concerning Stalker himself, and how he's an analogue for Tarkovsky, and for artists as a whole. 

Stalker takes people on a path that others ask him to taken them on, leading them down a seemingly random, complicated, and ever changing path to an end that results in the traveler to assume their own realization and meaning from the end. 

Everyday life is sepia, essentially black and white, controlled, authoritarian. The Zone is colorful, breaming with mystery and intrigue, unpredictable. We escape into art, and film specifically, to be put on a path that we can't know the true end of until we reach it. We have an idea of what we could expect, but until you take the journey and see the end for yourself, you can never know what it holds.

Stalker is Tarkovsky, and again perhaps all artists, bemoaning the lack of faith of the viewer, for their lack of curiosity, and their cynicism. Going to the Zone/the art with only selfishness. It's implied that some of those who come with an open mind are met more kindly than those who come for personal gain. Some, but not all. 

This isn't a be-all-end-all interpretation by any means, what makes the film so wonderful is it works on so many different levels. But this trail of thought really got me energized, and the ways that it works across most, if not all, of the film. 

Art and society and personal and cultural enrichment go hand-in-hand.
